notes:
Lead background: small support SaaS (ticketing + chat widget) targeting ecom merchants. Signed up via self-serve, using hosted API. Primary pain: perceived latency from EU customers after they integrated the chat widget (avg p95 reported ~700-900ms, goal p95 <300-400ms for core UX). Strong cost sensitivity; want to avoid moving to Dedicated for now — prefer tuning in hosted tier.

Customer comments / paraphrases: "Users abandon chat if reply takes >1s"; "We like the simple API but need guidance on timeouts and region choice".

Technical notes & observed patterns: - Most traffic originates in NA (60%) and EU (35%), EU traffic hits NA region endpoint currently (they left default). - Typical prompts: short chat context + 3-5 KB of recent messages; sometimes include long product descriptions (payloads up to 2k tokens). - Concurrency: front-end opens 20-30 concurrent requests during peak; each request uses streaming. - Model preference: prefer small/fast open models (quantized 7B or 13B low-latency variants).

Quick SE recommendations given in call: - Use region-specific endpoints (eu.redwood.ai) for EU users to cut cross-region RTT. - Increase client-side timeout to 30s from 10s for streaming to avoid premature cancellations; set HTTP keep-alive and connection pooling. - Reduce prompt length and send heavy context as embeddings + retrieval for long product data. - Enable streaming chunk size to render partial tokens earlier in UI; set server-sent-event buffer low. - Try a low-latency model variant (e.g., 7B quantized) for first-pass replies and fallback to higher-quality model for follow-up async improvements. - Set max_tokens conservatively and use stop sequences to shorten tail generation. - Leverage Redwood Optimize suggestions: batching windows and prefix caching for common greetings to reduce per-token cost.

POC plan (agreed on call): 1) SE to provision a test key scoped to eu+na endpoints; run 2-day simulated load with 100 concurrent users to measure p50/p95. 2) SE to send perf-tuning quickstart (drive:/playbooks/perf-tuning-quickstart.md) and a short checklist for prompt hygiene. 3) Customer to implement region routing in front-end and report metrics. 4) Post-POC: evaluate need for Dedicated or specific routing policies.

Open items / questions: - They asked whether Redwood enforces any default client-side timeouts (answer: no, defaults depend on SDK; recommended 30s for streaming). - Need clarification on EU data residency; they currently think they must store transcripts in EU — asked for security FAQ. - Pricing sensitivity: want clear per-token cost for low-latency model variants to compare to vector-retrieval costs.

Next steps (short): Marcus to schedule 30-min POC kickoff (link in Gmail thread thread-AP8f3x9JPMxQ). Send customized estimate and perf tuning checklist. Follow up in 4 business days for status.
